summary: Post-handshake cross-region egress queueing causing APAC inference tail latency and timeouts
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 03:15 UTC BrightCart (enterprise customer) reported elevated p95/p99 inference latencies and a rise in 504s originating from APAC clients. Symptoms show TLS handshakes complete successfully but application-level responses stall; many requests become queued and either time out or incur 20–60s tails. This ticket captures triage, investigation notes, and mitigation actions.
impact: Customer-facing inference features for BrightCart in APAC experienced p99 latency increases from ~800ms to 18–45s and ~12% request timeouts for streaming/generation endpoints. Multiple SLAs are at risk; several customers reported user-visible errors during a marketing campaign peak window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use BrightCart account token scoped to apac-southeast-1. 2) Send concurrent streaming generate requests (batch of 50 clients, ~5 RPS each) with sequence length ~1024. 3) Observe initial TLS handshake and then long queue times in downstream proxy for many requests; p99 latency spikes and some streams report 'stream cancelled' client-side. 4) Reproduce is intermittent and more likely under sustained concurrent load.
logs: Collected artifacts: envoy downstream_cluster metrics (queue_time_histogram spikes 20000–45000ms), egress-proxy logs with repeated upstream connect attempts, per-request trace IDs (list attached in Confluence). TLS logs show handshake completes at t0, first application bytes not seen until t0+seconds. No obvious 5xx during handshake stage. Kernel-level tcp retransmits low; path appears healthy until post-handshake proxying.
investigation_notes: - Timeline: Spike first visible 2026-03-10 02:58 UTC; BrightCart reported at 03:15 UTC. - SRE checked POP health: local APAC POPs healthy; packet-level metrics show ARP/BGP stable. - Traces show requests complete TLS but then hand off to upstream cluster 'egress-global-us-east' instead of local 'egress-apac-southeast'. - Routing-service recently rolled out weight-based egress rewrite (2026-03-09 23:40 UTC) to support account-level egress preferences; rollout included a config that rewrites SNI/account tag for accounts flagged with 'global-egress' during a migration. - Egress-proxy v2.4.1 introduced a change in upstream selection: if local cluster reports >x active streams it rewrites to fallback cluster and queues requests waiting for connection; combined with prefix rewrite this triggered cross-region handoff. - Hypothesis: the new routing rewrite + egress-proxy fallback logic caused a subset of BrightCart traffic to be proxied cross-region (APAC -> us-east) after TLS handshake, introducing network RTT + downstream queueing and KV-cache cold misses in serving runtime, leading to long tails and timeouts.
comments: 2026-03-10 03:22 - Maya Chen (Support): 'Customer reports elevated p99s and 504s. Collected request IDs and initial traces. Escalating to SRE and Eng.'

2026-03-10 03:35 - SRE (A. Patel): 'Confirmed traces show post-handshake hop to us-east egress cluster for ~17% of BrightCart requests. Local egress capacity looks nominal; investigating routing rewrite config.'

2026-03-10 04:05 - Eng (Liam O'Connor): 'Found recent routing-service config change that tags BrightCart for global-egress during migration. Rolling back tag for BrightCart as an immediate mitigation. Will work with egress-proxy team on retry/fallback semantics.'

2026-03-10 04:40 - Support (Maya Chen): 'Customer observed latency drop after rollback; p99 returned to ~900ms for monitored endpoints. Customer still seeing occasional 5s tails; continuing to monitor.'

2026-03-10 10:12 - Eng (S. Gupta): 'PR created to patch egress-proxy fallback behavior to avoid cross-region handoff post-handshake: https://github.com/redwood-inference/egress-proxy/pull/345. Also adding a routing-service guard to prefer local POP when RTT delta < 30ms.'
resolution: Mitigation applied: rolled back account-level global-egress tag for BrightCart at 2026-03-10 03:50 UTC, which removed cross-region handoff for the majority of traffic. Patch PR#345 applied to egress-proxy to change fallback behavior and avoid post-handshake cluster rewrite; hotfix deployment scheduled to 2026-03-11 05:00 UTC canary, 06:00 UTC full roll. Follow-ups: add a canary gate to routing-service rollouts, add alerting on post-handshake cluster switch rate, document playbook in Confluence and notify impacted customers. Customer confirmed partial recovery; monitoring continues. This ticket will be closed after hotfix verified in APAC and no recurrence for 72 hours.
next_steps: 1) Deploy egress-proxy hotfix and monitor. 2) Add routing-service guard and unit tests to prevent account tag misassignment during rollouts. 3) Add metric and alert: 'post_handshake_cluster_switch_rate' > 0.5% triggers auto-triage. 4) Coordinate with BrightCart CS for follow-up review and SLA credit if SLA breached. 5) Draft final incident report and distribute to GTM and Eng leadership.
